source_meta._title: Leads in unloaded chunks break, become invisible or connect to an invisible target far away

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition Snapshot 13w17a in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world. Use default controls where possible. The Superflat world, Creative mode, a cow, and reduced render distance are practical choices for creating and unloading the test arrangement without crafting, exploration, combat, or terrain obstacles; the report does not require those exact choices.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Snapshot 13w17a; do not use either listed fix version, Minecraft 15w31b or 1.15 Pre-release 1.
Use an unmodified vanilla client with no mods or external server software that could alter entity or chunk-loading behavior.
Create a disposable world because this reproduction deliberately tests historical snapshot behavior.
The executor must be able to use Creative inventory and Creative flight.
Use a leashable animal. This plan selects a cow as a simple representative of the report's stated 'any animals' condition.
Place the test site well away from the initial world-spawn area so spawn-chunk loading is less likely to keep the animal's chunk active.
Perform one unload-and-return cycle initially. The report describes the issue as occurring 'most of the times,' so one clean cycle does not establish that the setup was invalid.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact historical version listed as "Snapshot 13w17a", start it, and wait for the main menu. Do not substitute a later release or either fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed game version identifies 13w17a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set World Type to Superflat, and create the world. Leave the seed unspecified because the report supplies no required seed.
steps.success_cue: World generation has started with Creative mode and the Superflat world type selected.

steps.action: Wait without opening another menu until the world is visible, nearby flat terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a fully rendered area of the Superflat world.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, and click the Render Distance setting until it reads Tiny. Return to the world. The historical Far, Normal, Short, and Tiny render-distance labels and their era-appropriate ranges were externally checked. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3AServer.properties/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The world is active again and distant terrain is hidden by the short Tiny render distance.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug display. Read and record the player's initial X and Z coordinates as spawn-reference coordinates. Ignore Y for the horizontal-distance calculations.
steps.success_cue: The debug display is visible and the initial X and Z values have been recorded.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight by double-tapping the Jump control, whose default key is Space. Hold the Forward control, whose default key is W, and travel horizontally until the current position is at least 320 blocks from the recorded initial position along X, Z, or their combined horizontal displacement.
steps.success_cue: The F3 coordinates show that the player is at least 320 horizontal blocks from the initial position.

steps.action: Descend using the Sneak control, whose default key is Left Shift, until standing on the flat ground. Wait until the local terrain is fully rendered and movement is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on stable ground at a test site at least 320 blocks from the initial position.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab if available and place one Fence, one Lead, and one cow spawn egg into separate hotbar slots. In this historical version, use the single wooden item named Fence rather than a modern wood-specific fence name. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: A Fence, a Lead, and a cow spawn egg are visible in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the Fence's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim at the top surface of a nearby grass block and press the Use Item control, whose default input is right-click, once to place the fence.
steps.success_cue: One upright fence post is present at the test site.

steps.action: Select the cow spawn egg. Aim at an open grass block approximately 2 to 4 blocks horizontally from the fence and right-click once to spawn a cow.
steps.success_cue: One living cow is present near the fence with an unobstructed path between the cow and fence.

steps.action: Select the Lead in the hotbar, move within interaction range of the cow, aim directly at the cow, and right-click it once to attach the held lead.
steps.success_cue: A lead line visibly connects the player to the cow while the player remains near it.

steps.action: While the cow remains attached to the held lead, walk to the fence, aim directly at the fence post, and right-click the fence once to tie the lead to it.
steps.success_cue: The lead now runs between the cow and the fence, and a lead knot is visible on the fence post.

steps.action: Stop moving for several seconds and confirm only the setup state: the cow remains close to the fence, the lead is visibly attached at both ends, and neither endpoint is near the lead's maximum stretched distance. Do not yet leave the area.
steps.success_cue: A stable cow-to-fence lead arrangement is present before any chunk unloading occurs.

steps.action: With F3 still open, record the fence's approximate X and Z coordinates as the return coordinates. If F3 was closed, press F3 before recording them.
steps.success_cue: The test site's X and Z return coordinates have been recorded.

steps.action: Face directly away from the test site and enter Creative flight by double-tapping Space. Ascend several blocks so fences or minor terrain cannot obstruct horizontal travel.
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne and can travel away from the cow-and-fence test site without ground obstacles.

steps.action: Fly horizontally away from the recorded test-site coordinates. Continue until F3 shows a horizontal displacement of at least 512 blocks from the test site. Do not merely fly upward above the same X and Z position; the player must leave the test area's horizontal chunk-loading range.
steps.exact_input: Hold W until horizontal distance is at least 512 blocks
steps.success_cue: The recorded test site is not visible, and the current X/Z position is at least 512 horizontal blocks from it.

steps.action: Remain at the distant location for at least 10 seconds with the game unpaused. Wait until nearby destination chunks have rendered and player movement responds normally before returning.
steps.success_cue: The player has remained over 512 blocks away for at least 10 unpaused seconds and the destination area is fully responsive.

steps.action: Turn toward the recorded test-site coordinates and fly back horizontally. Use the F3 X and Z values to correct direction as needed, keeping the return coordinates centered as the distance decreases.
steps.exact_input: Hold W and navigate toward the recorded X/Z coordinates
steps.success_cue: The player's horizontal distance from the recorded test site is steadily decreasing.

steps.action: Continue approaching until the terrain at the recorded test-site coordinates transitions from outside the rendered area into view. Do not interact with the cow, fence, ground, or any dropped item during this approach.
steps.success_cue: The block terrain containing the recorded test site has just re-entered rendered view after being taken at least 512 blocks out of range.

steps.action: Stop close enough to view the test site, and wait only until its surrounding terrain has finished rendering and movement responds normally. Do not right-click the animal or fence and do not pick up or break anything; preserve the freshly reloaded state for the Observation Agent.
steps.success_cue: The recorded cow-and-fence test area is fully rendered and responsive after the unload-and-return cycle, with no post-return interaction performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just returned from at least 512 blocks away, the chunk containing the previously verified cow-to-fence lead arrangement has re-entered rendered view, surrounding terrain has finished loading, and the player has not interacted with or altered the setup since returning. Begin observation of the freshly reloaded lead arrangement.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, world type, animal species, render distance, exact unload distance, or exact unload duration. Creative mode, Superflat terrain, a cow, Tiny render distance, a site at least 320 blocks from the initial spawn position, a 512-block departure, and a 10-second distant wait are practical execution choices rather than report requirements.

The issue combines multiple possible manifestations after unloading and reloading. This plan reproduces only their common setup and trigger and intentionally does not classify which manifestation, if any, occurred.

The report states that an occurrence happens 'most of the times,' so the behavior is intermittent. If the Observation Agent records no occurrence, a later independent trial may recreate a fresh cow-to-fence attachment and repeat the unload cycle; repeated triggering is not included in the initial plan.
The exact launcher navigation used to expose historical snapshots can vary by launcher release. Regardless of launcher UI, the game process must identify itself as 13w17a before execution continues.

External verification was limited to the historical render-distance labels and approximate era-specific ranges. The Mojira report remains the source for the actual lead attachment and chunk-unload trigger.
